source_title: The 6 Best Books Set In Video Games, Ranked
source_excerpt:
Ever since Atari's Pong brought gaming into people's living rooms in the early 70s, video games have continued to evolve and become an important part of pop culture. Naturally, this has inspired plenty of books about video games over the years. Video games are a great foundation to build compelling, thought-provoking narratives from, and literature has been the home of some of the best stories on the subject.
Some of these books use video games as a backdrop to highlight a larger subject, but there are also a few incredibly clever books that use staple video game tropes and logic to create a wild page-turner. From the serious to the wonderfully goofy, books about video games have taken many shapes and forms.
The following list excludes manga and comic books.
A Solid YA Intro To Video Game Fiction
Authors : Jason Segel, Kirsten Miller
That's right, Jason Segel from How I Met Your Mother , Forgetting Sarah Marshall , and The Muppets co-wrote a YA novel with Kirsten Miller, and it's all about a virtual reality world with a dark secret. Otherworld is a story about a teenager named Simon who finds himself obsessed with an innovative and ambitious virtual reality game that fully immerses the player into the experience.
However, the game that Simon has become so infatuated with isn't exactly just an innocent game. Segel and Miller bring forth a lot of humor and intrigue with this story, but it's also a fairly one-dimensional view of video games. The titular Otherworld game is a tool that helps raise interesting questions about escapism and the unrestrained power that virtual worlds allow people to have. It's a great starter book for this specific fiction niche and a solid sci-fi YA novel for younger readers.
This is also a great starter for younger gamers who want to get into reading. Epic follows a boy named Erik Haraldson who lives in a world where the world's conflicts are dealt with in an MMORPG game, since the planet has banned real-world violence. That sounds ideal on the surface, but a player's success or failure in the game determines their social status in real life.
Imagine a world where some of the best fantasy MMORPGs like World of Warcraft and RuneScape dictate whether you have a good life or not. It's a clever premise, but it might not be the best choice for readers who are looking for something with a lot of video game depth. Like Otherworld , Epic 's premise uses gaming as a way to highlight real-world issues like class divides.
This is the video game book that most gamers know about. Even non-gamers know about Ready Player One . Ernest Cline's novel was a massive hit, and it even inspired a Ready Player One movie directed by the one and only Steven Spielberg. Cline's story made way for one of the coolest sci-fi movie worlds of the past decade, but the book is even better.
Ready Player One 's story is set in the mid 2040s, and life on Earth has become less than desirable. Protagonist Wade Watts spends his days escaping in an immersive virtual reality game world known as the OASIS. Here, players from around the globe join in and try to find the secret in-game treasure hidden by the game's creator. If Wade solves all the creator's clues, he could unlock an immense amount of power. Ready Player One is a fun, high-energy love letter to pop culture, which makes it a quick read.
In hindsight, the book's focus on large-scale gaming communities and pop culture references also feels like it predicted games like Fortnite .

One of the coolest things about Bedlam is that it's the one game on this list that actually has an actual tie-in video game that you can play. The game shares the same title, and author Christopher Brookmyre also served as its writer. Bedlam 's story follows Ross Baker, a scientist working for a giant tech company who has grown incredibly burnt out with his lackluster job.
In order to shake up the mundanity of office life, Ross offers to be a test subject for the company's new brain tech. However, things go wrong when he finds himself transported into one of his favorite FPS games from childhood with no way out. The fictional game takes inspiration from classic 90s FPS games , and it uses the staple tropes and level design of this era and turns them into great narrative devices.
The Apocalypse, But With Dungeon Crawling
Dungeon Crawler Carl might not technically take place inside a video game, but the setting is deeply inspired by the many great dungeon crawler games that have helped shape this particular corner of the industry. In Dungeon Crawler Carl , the titular Carl finds himself in a truly tough situation; an alien civilization has invaded Earth and has transformed the planet's landscape into a subterranean dungeon. That's only the tip of the iceberg of Carl's problem, though. The aliens have turned this new dungeon-ified version of Earth into a televised obstacle course reality show, forcing Carl to fight through some truly ridiculous scenarios in order to stay alive.
Thankfully, Carl isn't alone. His ex-girlfriend's cat, Princess Donut, is also along for the journey. It's a wonderfully absurd story that has spanned an entire series. Author Matt Dinniman originally self-published the first book, which makes its evolution that much more intriguing. Dinniman has a great understanding of what makes dungeon crawlers so fun and strange when thrown into a real-life context, and there is even a live-action TV series being produced for Peacock.
1 Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
A Love Letter To Video Games And Creativity
This is another one that doesn't exactly take place inside a video game, but it does dive into the complexities of game development. So, technically, it's set within a video game, just from a development standpoint. Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow is far more than that, though. The story follows Sam and Sadie, once childhood friends who reconnect in college. This reunion kickstarts a whirlwind lifelong partnership, as the duo becomes creative partners who craft successful video games.
I won't dive too deep into this book, because it's too special to spoil, but Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow is a beautifully written tale that dives into themes of platonic friendships, the power of creativity, ambition, and why exactly video games are such an important form of entertainment.
